Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]) and let $H$ be a nonzero complex Hilbert space ([[def-hilbert-space]]). Recall that $T_{u,v}\in\mathcal B(H)$ denotes the rank-one operator $T_{u,v}x=\langle x,v\rangle u$ ([[lem-nrqm-composites-rank-one-operator-calculus]]).

(a) A **density operator** on $H$ is a self-adjoint positive trace-class operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=1$ ([[def-trace-class-operator]], [[def-trace-of-a-trace-class-operator]], [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]). If $(u_n)_{n\in J}$ is a finite or countable orthonormal family, with $J$ a finite initial segment of the positive integers or all positive integers, and $w_n\ge0$ with $\sum_nw_n=1$, then the sum $\rho:=\sum_nw_nT_{u_n,u_n}$ converges in trace norm to a density operator with $\operatorname{tr}\rho=\sum_nw_n=1$. Conversely every density operator $\rho$ admits such an expansion whose weights are its positive eigenvalues counted with multiplicity and whose vectors are orthonormal eigenvectors; distinct expansions of the same $\rho$ exist when a positive eigenspace has dimension at least two.

(b) Let $E$ be a projection-valued measure on a measurable space $(X,\Sigma)$ acting on $H$ ([[def-projection-valued-measure]]). Then $\mu_\rho(B):=\operatorname{tr}(\rho E(B))$ is a well-defined probability measure on $(X,\Sigma)$ ([[def-measure]], [[def-probability-measure]]); it is given by the absolutely convergent series $\mu_\rho(B)=\sum_nw_n\|E(B)u_n\|^2$ in every expansion of (a), and reduces to $\mu_\rho(B)=\|E(B)u\|^2$ for a pure density operator $\rho=T_{u,u}$ with $\|u\|=1$.

(c) Assume in addition the Axiom of Choice ([[def-axiom-of-choice]]). Let $A$ be a self-adjoint operator with projection-valued measure $E_A$ ([[thm-spectral-theorem-for-unbounded-self-adjoint-operators]]) and let $\psi\in H$ have $\|\psi\|=1$ and $\psi\in D(A)$. Here $|A|^{1/2}$ denotes the unbounded PVM integral $f(E_A)$ for $f(\lambda)=|\lambda|^{1/2}$, with domain $D(f(E_A))=\{\psi:\int |\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}<\infty\}$ as in [[def-unbounded-integral-against-a-pvm]]. Then

$$\int_{\mathbb R}\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\langle A\psi,\psi\rangle,\qquad \int_{\mathbb R}\lambda^2\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)=\|A\psi\|^2 ,$$

where $E_{A,\psi}(B)=\langle E_A(B)\psi,\psi\rangle$ ([[lem-scalar-and-complex-measures-from-a-pvm]]); moreover $\int_{\mathbb R}|\lambda|\,dE_{A,\psi}(\lambda)<\infty$ exactly when $\psi\in D(|A|^{1/2})$, and then the mean $\int\lambda\,dE_{A,\psi}$ is finite. No product $A\rho$ of an unbounded operator with a density operator is used, and no physical interpretation of $\mu_\rho$ or of the moments is asserted.

derivations.claim: [Computational basis decomposition] By [A3], $\frac12T_{e_1,e_1}+\frac12T_{e_2,e_2}$ has matrix $\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}+\frac12\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&1\end{pmatrix}=\frac12 I$, and by [A2] it is a trace-class operator of trace $\frac12+\frac12=1$; by [A1] it is a density operator coming from the orthonormal family $(e_1,e_2)$ with weights $\frac12,\frac12$.

[Fixed $\pm$ basis decomposition] The vectors $e_\pm=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}(e_1\pm e_2)$ are unit and orthogonal since $\langle e_+,e_-\rangle=\frac12(\langle e_1,e_1\rangle-\langle e_1,e_2\rangle+\langle e_2,e_1\rangle-\langle e_2,e_2\rangle)=0$; their matrices are $T_{e_+,e_+}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}$ and $T_{e_-,e_-}=\frac12\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\-1&1\end{pmatrix}$, so $\frac12T_{e_+,e_+}+\frac12T_{e_-,e_-}=\frac12 I$ again, with weights $\frac12,\frac12$ on an orthonormal family; thus the same operator $\frac12 I$ has a second decomposition.

[The decompositions are different] The two orthonormal families are distinct: $|\langle e_1,e_+\rangle|=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\notin\{0,1\}$, so $e_1$ is not a scalar multiple of $e_\pm$ and $T_{e_1,e_1}$ is not one of $T_{e_\pm,e_\pm}$ (their matrices of step 2.1 differ from $\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$); hence the two lists of rank-one density operators are not the same up to reordering, while both convex combinations equal the single operator $\frac12 I$ by steps 1.1 and 2.1. Therefore this density operator has a nonunique orthonormal convex decomposition into rank-one density operators, consistent with the expansion in [A1].

Let $V,W$ be nonzero finite-dimensional complex inner product spaces with orthonormal bases $(e_1,\dots,e_m)$ of $V$ and $(f_1,\dots,f_n)$ of $W$, let $V\otimes W$ be their tensor product with the inner product of [[lem-nrqm-composites-hilbert-tensor-construction]], and let $\operatorname{tr}$ denote the basis-independent trace of an endomorphism ([[def-trace-of-an-endomorphism]]).

(a) For every endomorphism $R$ of $V\otimes W$ there is a unique endomorphism $\operatorname{Tr}_W R$ of $V$ with

$$\operatorname{tr}\bigl((\operatorname{Tr}_WR)A\bigr)=\operatorname{tr}\bigl(R(A\otimes I_W)\bigr)\qquad\text{for every }A\in\operatorname{End}(V),$$

namely $\operatorname{Tr}_WR=\sum_{j=1}^n\varphi_j\circ R\circ\iota_j$, where $\iota_j(v)=v\otimes f_j$ and $\varphi_j(x\otimes w)=\langle w,f_j\rangle x$; it does not depend on the orthonormal basis $(f_j)$ of $W$, and the analogous definition gives $\operatorname{Tr}_V R$ with $\operatorname{tr}((\operatorname{Tr}_VR)B)=\operatorname{tr}(R(I_V\otimes B))$.

(b) $\operatorname{Tr}_W$ is linear, positive (it maps positive endomorphisms to positive endomorphisms) and trace preserving on density matrices: if $R\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}R=1$ then $\operatorname{Tr}_WR\ge0$ and $\operatorname{tr}\operatorname{Tr}_WR=1$; and $\operatorname{Tr}_W T_{\Psi,\Psi}=CC^*$ for every $\Psi\in V\otimes W$, where $C:W\to V$ is the coefficient map determined by $\Psi=\sum_jCf_j\otimes f_j$.

(c) *Schmidt decomposition.* Every $\Psi\in V\otimes W$ admits an expansion

$$\Psi=\sum_{r=1}^{k}s_r\,v_r\otimes u_r,$$

with $k\le\min(m,n)$, orthonormal families $(v_r)\subseteq V$, $(u_r)\subseteq W$ and $s_1\ge\cdots\ge s_k>0$ uniquely determined by $\Psi$ as the positive singular values of the coefficient map; moreover $\|\Psi\|^2=\sum_rs_r^2$. For $\|\Psi\|=1$ the reduced density $\rho=\operatorname{Tr}_W T_{\Psi,\Psi}$ satisfies $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=\sum_rs_r^4$, and $\operatorname{tr}\rho^2=1$ holds exactly when $k=1$, i.e. exactly when $\Psi$ is a product vector; mixed-state separability is not decided by this criterion.

(d) *Finite nonselective no-signalling.* If $(M_a)_{a=1}^p$ are endomorphisms of $W$ with $\sum_aM_a^*M_a=I_W$ then for every endomorphism $R$ of $V\otimes W$

$$\operatorname{Tr}_W\Bigl(\sum_a(I_V\otimes M_a)R(I_V\otimes M_a^*)\Bigr)=\operatorname{Tr}_WR .$$

This is an identity for the specified finite local instrument; selective conditioning (dividing one summand by its nonzero trace) is not covered.

Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]). Let $H,K$ be complex Hilbert spaces, let $(M_a)_{a\ge1}$ be bounded operators on $K$ with $\sum_{a\le N}M_a^*M_a\to I_K$ strongly, and let $R$ be a trace-class operator on $H\widehat\otimes K$. In this statement, $R\ge0$ means that $R$ is self-adjoint and $\langle Rx,x\rangle\ge0$ for every $x$, as in [[def-self-adjoint-positive-unitary-and-normal-operator]]. Then the series (when either factor is $\{0\}$, use the zero partial-trace maps $\operatorname{Tr}_K:\mathcal S_1(\{0\})\to\mathcal S_1(H)$ and $\operatorname{Tr}_H:\mathcal S_1(\{0\})\to\mathcal S_1(K)$; when both factors are nonzero, use the partial traces of [[lem-nrqm-composites-separable-partial-trace]])

$$\sum_{a\ge1}(I_H\otimes M_a)R(I_H\otimes M_a^*)$$

converges in trace norm, its sum $\Phi(R)$ is trace class with $\operatorname{tr}\Phi(R)=\operatorname{tr}R$ and $\Phi(R)\ge0$ if $R\ge0$, and the reduced state on $H$ is unchanged:

$$\operatorname{Tr}_K\Phi(R)=\operatorname{Tr}_KR .$$

By symmetry, a local map $R\mapsto\sum_a(N_a\otimes I_K)R(N_a^*\otimes I_K)$ on the first factor also leaves $\operatorname{Tr}_HR$ fixed. Selective conditioning (one summand normalized by its nonzero trace) is not covered.

derivations.claim: [The instrument] On $K$ take the self-adjoint projections $M_0:=P_0=T_{e_-,e_-}$ and $M_1:=P_1=T_{e_+,e_+}$, so that $M_a^*M_a=P_a$ for $a=0,1$ and $\sum_aM_a^*M_a=P_0+P_1=I_K$: this is the stipulated Lüders instrument for the sharp observable $P_0$. Its outcome-$0$ non-normalized conditional operator on $H\otimes K$ is $(I\otimes P_0)\rho(I\otimes P_0)$.

[The selected outcome] Let $\Psi_0:=(I\otimes P_0)\Psi=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}e_+\otimes e_-$. Its coefficient map in the chosen bases has matrix $C_0=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$. The outcome probability is $\operatorname{tr}\bigl((I\otimes P_0)\rho(I\otimes P_0)\bigr)=\|\Psi_0\|^2=\frac12>0$, and the non-normalized conditional operator is $T_{\Psi_0,\Psi_0}=\frac12T_{e_+\otimes e_-,e_+\otimes e_-}$. After normalization the conditional state is $T_{e_+\otimes e_-,e_+\otimes e_-}$.

[The conditional reduced state differs] The coefficient map of the unit vector $e_+\otimes e_-$ has one nonzero matrix entry, equal to $1$ in the $e_+$ row and $e_-$ column, so its product with its adjoint is $T_{e_+,e_+}$. By [L1], the conditional reduced state on $H$ is therefore $\operatorname{Tr}_K T_{e_+\otimes e_-,e_+\otimes e_-}=T_{e_+,e_+}$. The unconditional reduced state is $\operatorname{Tr}_K\rho=CC^*$ for the coefficient matrix $C=\frac{1}{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\-1&0\end{pmatrix}$ of $\Psi$, namely $\frac12 I_H$. These differ, since $\langle T_{e_+,e_+}e_+,e_+\rangle=1\ne\frac12=\langle\frac12 I_He_+,e_+\rangle$. Hence the selective conditional reduced state is not the unconditional one, and the claim of [L3] fails for this unit vector and instrument.

[The nonselective identity still holds] The outcome-$1$ summand is $(I\otimes P_1)\rho(I\otimes P_1)$, and $(I\otimes P_1)\Psi=-\frac{1}{\sqrt2}e_-\otimes e_+$, so this summand equals $\frac12T_{e_-\otimes e_+,e_-\otimes e_+}$. The coefficient map of the unit vector $e_-\otimes e_+$ has one nonzero entry in the $e_-$ row, so its reduced state on $H$ is $T_{e_-,e_-}$ by [L1]. Adding both summands and using the linearity of $\operatorname{Tr}_K$ [L2] gives $\operatorname{Tr}_K\bigl(\sum_a(I\otimes M_a)\rho(I\otimes M_a^*)\bigr)=\frac12T_{e_+,e_+}+\frac12T_{e_-,e_-}=\frac12 I_H=\operatorname{Tr}_K\rho$, in agreement with the nonselective identity of [L2]. The refuted claim is thus exactly the illegitimate replacement of that nonselective identity by its selective counterpart.
